To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

self-injected electrons from the channel walls in a plasma channel with a density of 3.2×1019 cm-3 are accelerated to 0.26 and 0.84GeV after a distance of 0.55 and 0.85cm, respectively, and that a laser pulse with an initial energy of 0,4J is reduced to 0.05J after 0.85 cm.
self-injection in a centimeter long plasma channel leads to monoenergetic bunches of electrons with energies in the GeV range.
the laser wakefield accelerator (LWFA) can be extended to the GeV range using plasma channel guiding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of high-energy electron acceleration in laser-plasma interactions.
the development of a new generation of compact particle accelerators based on the interaction of intense laser pulses with plasma.
laser wakefield acceleration of electrons in a plasma channel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the first bunch is accelerated by the wakefield generated in the channel, while the second one by the laser wakefield.
the laser pulse has been accelerated by the laser pulse.
the laser pulse has been stretched to a duration of 0.5 ps (FWHM) and the energy of the accelerated electrons has been increased from 100 MeV to 1 GeV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the self-injected electrons can be accelerated to energies of 0.84-GeV with a 0.8-cm-long plasma channel and a 50-fs (FWHM) laser pulse with a peak intensity of 2×1018 W/cm2.
we can accelerate electrons to near-GeV-energy in a centimeter scale plasma channel with a laser pulse of 50 fs FWHM duration.
the self-injection of a monoenergetic electron bunch with a central energy up to 0,5 GeV can be achieved by using a 50 fs long laser pulse in a plasma channel with a length of 1 cm.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the self-injection of a highly localized electron bunch is a viable alternative to the injection of a pre-accelerated electron bunch for the generation of monoenergetic electron bunches in laser wakefield acceleration.

the self-injection mechanism in a plasma channel is not only a viable mechanism for laser-wakefield electron acceleration, but that the acceleration of a single bunch of electrons to near-GeV energies is possible in a 0 cm long plasma channel.
a single laser pulse can be used to accelerate two bunches of electrons to high energies in a centimeter scale plasma channel.
